question.problem: Using the method of orthogonal transformations, find the canonical form of $Q(x)=7{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{2}^{2}+5{x}_{3}^{2}-4{x}_{2}{x}_{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Every quadratic form can be reduced to its canonical (diagonal) form using orthogonal transformations.

To find the coefficients of the canonical form, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )((8-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-4) & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +36) & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(\lambda -4)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,7,\,4\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, writing the eigenvalues in descending order, we obtain the diagonal matrix

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

The corresponding quadratic form after a change of variables is

$$
9{y}_{1}^{2}+7{y}_{2}^{2}+4{y}_{3}^{2}.
$$
